llm.summary: The skill's code broadly matches its stated purpose (RunPod image/video generation) but contains mismatches and packaging oddities (missing declared requirements, an unusual 'uv' binary, and writable endpoint registry) that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, SKILL.md, and scripts all implement RunPod image/video functionality and legitimately need a RunPod API key and (when uploading local files) an imgbb API key. However, registry metadata provided earlier said 'no required env vars/binaries' while the included _meta.json and scripts require secrets and reference a 'uv' binary — an inconsistency in declared vs actual requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts mostly stay within the stated purpose: calling RunPod endpoints, uploading local images to imgbb, saving outputs to ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media, and optionally adding endpoints to the bundled endpoints.json. The SKILL.md correctly warns that local images uploaded to imgbb become public. One scope-related behavior to note: discover_endpoints has an 'add' mode that writes new entries into scripts/endpoints.json (modifies the skill's registry file).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), which is low-risk for external code downloads. However the package declares a runtime dependency on a nonstandard CLI 'uv' (run.sh execs 'uv run <script>.py'), and scripts declare a Python dependency ('requests') but no installer is provided. The 'uv' requirement is unusual and may cause runtime failures or confusion; packaging metadata (_meta.json) lists 'uv' while top-level registry metadata omitted it — inconsistent and risky for reliability.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code requires a RunPod API key and uses an imgbb API key when local files are provided; both are directly related to the documented functionality. The skill reads ~/.openclaw/secrets.json and environment variables RUNPOD_API_KEY / IMGBB_API_KEY, as documented in SKILL.md. The earlier registry summary that claimed 'no required env vars' is inaccurate — that's an inconsistency to address before trusting the skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated system privileges or 'always: true'. It writes outputs to ~/.openclaw/workspace/runpod-media and discover_endpoints 'add' can write to scripts/endpoints.json inside the skill bundle (modifies its own files). This behavior is within the skill's domain but merits user awareness because it can persist added endpoint IDs for future runs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to implement RunPod image/video functionality, but there are packaging and metadata inconsistencies you should clear up before installing: 1) Confirm how to run the scripts locally — run.sh uses a nonstandard 'uv' CLI; verify whether 'uv' is intentionally required or should be 'python' (and ensure 'requests' is installed). 2) Provide a RunPod API key and (if you will pass local files) an imgbb API key — understand that any local image uploaded via imgbb becomes publicly accessible. 3) Be aware that the discover_endpoints add mode will modify the skill's endpoints.json (it can persist unverified endpoint IDs); review entries before and after using that feature. 4) The skill's source is 'unknown' and homepage is none — if you plan to use it with real/paid API keys, prefer code from a known/trusted author or inspect/run the scripts in a controlled environment first. If the maintainer can clarify the 'uv' requirement and update the registry metadata to match _meta.json / SKILL.md, that would raise confidence.
